JMPD K-9 Operation

By: Sasha OLD | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

Unique Selling Point:
STORY OUTLINE and TREATMENT
So we all think the JMPD are corrupt traffic cops who wreck their cars. But here’s where you’re wrong - the metro cops actually have several tactical reaction and crime prevention units - one of them is the K9 unit - the one with the longest wait list and where all the tops cops are. We embedded with this unit for a month to see how they are protecting us. Their offices are hidden in nearby their headquarters in joburg city, there are roughly 6 teams (Alpha, bravo, charlie, delta, echo 1 and echo 2.) - lead by SuperIntendent Mahomed Hussein - he will be our main character. With more than 20 years in the force, he commands the respect of his peers as well as Chief Khanyile. His family have had to go into hiding, he’s been shot at, attacked and combatted nearly every crime joburg has to offer. Because of the nature of their work some of the officers from the Echo Units will need to be hidden, but they have consented to us filming their lower jaws to see them speaking, and with all the action I don’t think it’s something that detracts from the story. The echo units are the top cops - they are plain clothed officers who also move in unmarked vehicles which allows them to move in on the criminals easier than the other 4 units who are uniformed.


Summary:
We will have a link with Macfarlane where we say that we are being responsible and want to protect these officers as some of them like another one of our main characters “Rabbit” are being targeted by criminals they have been brought to book. Rabbit’s nephew was murdered because of him arresting some criminals, and they have planned two hits on him since. He has a wicked sense of humour, but is often in all the action - with 15 years experience - he is one of the best in echo 1. Then there is Links - Lincoln Moloi - from echo 2, he is a spokesperson at every scene and always comes prepared. He often works double shifts and is one of the most dedicated officers - a little shy, but trusted by the community - he is known for always having information from informers and being first on the scene. “Nike” - he is the sergeant of echo 2 - 15 years experience, he has been with the unit since its inception and leads the pack from the front. He is known as the top dog, he always travels with Sheeba his border collie who he calls a police officer. He can be emotional, but is a protector - who has 4 daughters and bears the responsibility of doing all the paperwork, as well as being front and centre on most scenes. Besides these 3 of echo 1 and 2 - there are others who appear in the story - Younos and Papas - known as the terrible twins or bac-and-teria. Magubane and Sitzwe - another unbreakable partnership. Vilakazi, Vence, Zwane and Natta (a female indian officer who roles with the boys).





Further information:
Then the officers who are uniformed - “Cherry Pie” - who is a tough female officer who takes no nonsense and decided to leave the echo units to become a uniformed officer because it requires a 24.7 approach. She has been with the unit roughly 14 years and her Golden Retriever Fire is a stud when it comes to competing, as well as sniffing out narcotics. Then there is Tyrone Moitze - a 6.8 towering giant. He and his german shepherd wolf are one of my main characters, he speaks to camera without hidden identity and is loveable and hard working. Wolf sniffs out the guns and explosives at most scenes. We see his dog working, as well as competing. They really are a lovable pair. Then there is the Seppi - Saregent September who heads all the training of the dogs. His office is adorned with every award a dog trainer could ever behold and is fierce when it comes to whats best for his working animals.

Theme: broken window approach: We meet them at the mayors office - the members are briefed by super intendent mahomed hussein, and his sergeant - Nike. They are told that we are conducting a raid on an inner city hijacked building where the nearby business owners have complained about drug dealers illegally occupying and living in the building. We go in kicking in doors, searching suspects with the dogs. We recover several drugs with cooper a narcotics dog. We have great footage of searching the suspects etc. This is one of several operations in which the JMPD lead there members into treacherous and unknown circumstances. This is all part of the city’s call to clean up it’s streets - something that is hard to do because of a lack of resources like vehicles, red tape surrounding the laws allowing officers to protect themselves and of course the fact that Joburg is overrun with gangs who hijack vehicles, plague houses by robbing them and now a new crime - kidnapping. On another night, we raid several johannesburg buildings - find drugs, and over 50 illegals are sent to lindela. We have footage of the illegals being put into vans - its very sad - then we show their living conditions - which are horrendous. We then break down the door of the one room, and a guy jumps out the window. He’s the one on the news that died.
Theme: Often police are targeted: like when a member house was targeted and his firearm was stolen (CCTV footage), we got information about the cars locations through informers, so we watched the car for two nights - and then we caught them with the gun - nice footage of arrests. They track cell phones - and we recovered a police cellphone that was stolen in KZN in soweto - we then searched the suspects house for the gun. We used Moitze and Wolf who sniffs throughout the house looking for the weapon. A police officer was attacked in joburg for his firearm, three days later after observation we manage to catch the criminals with the firearm after a chase. Very exciting footage. Then one night we get the call that a fellow JMPD officer has been targeted and shot dead. Supe gives a very emotional speech about this, and we will hear from Rabbit about how he has these hits out for him.
Theme: Crime Prevention: What most people don’t know is that Echo 1 and 2 are crime prevention experts - riding around every day and night fighting crime before it happens - like in the case of the armed robbery we were all seemingly prepared to stop before we ran into it and there was a shoot out, in which rabbit and nike emptied their clips within minutes. Nike gave chase on foot, while Rabbit tried to catch one of the gettaway vehicles. By the end of the explosive fight, two suspects died from bullet wounds and the boys survived - just barely to catch the cars and recover the alcohol. Rabbit and Nike were very emotional afterwards having just had a gun fight with roughly 15 armed suspects - they will talk us through what happened, and we also have the CCTV footage and chase following the shootout.

Crime response: We have several chases resulting in vehicle recoveries and arrests - action (3 suspects arrested with two vehicles, orange farm chase and arrest, sometimes the cars are abandoned. We assist in capturing a murderer who killed two women - we get him on the highway. We execute an arrest warrant on an armed robber - nice CCTV footage of him robbing house.

Expected the unexpected crimes
One night we are chased by a naked guy, we ran into the prostitutes under the joe slovo bridge who see our cameras and run away... Supe gets out to stop a fight and gets hit by a brick, and one night we capture a young teen who tried to stab a madala, and the madala taught him a lesson by getting the knife and stabbing him several times - the boy poops his pants and fake cries. It’s great! One night we caught boys with drugs - and Nike popped the khat out of the guys mouth. Then that guy lead us to his bosses house, where we happened to run into a group who had just stolen milk! Drugs - one day we went into joburg city to see how easily available drugs are - we catch multiple dealers selling Nyaope - and while we are doing that we also see a hijacker in the middle of a car theft - using scissors! I mean seriously!

Through these themes we will explore what it’s like to work with these officers, who talk us through how they work and show - NOT TELL - with action how they are protecting South Africans.

This story will be character and action driven - there’s a lot of thought and time that has gone into getting the goods before we shoot - so we can discuss how the story will look but I would think that it would easily hold for 20 minutes because here we have all the action, quiet moments, funny moments - it will be a Carte Blanche audience pleaser.

Petrol - travelling a lot every night

Script:


Gun shot! High speed chase - montage of action...

SUBTITLE: Johannesburg is a bustling city open for business, but that attracts criminals who target its residents...
While most sleep, members of the JMPD’s crack K9 unit leave their homes and families to patrol the city’s streets to prevent these criminals from taking over.

Sikalala: Don’t ask me questions! F**k (bleep) you!
With a long waiting list of officers who want to join their ranks, the K9 unit of Johannesburg’s Metro Police Department specializes in crime prevention.

Supe: “We are quite close to our target.”show bedroom visuals here

THEN LEAD INTO THE HERO VISUALS Super-in-tendent Mahomed Hoosen - called Supe - joined the police in his twenties. A father of two, he wanted to make the city safe for his family. He now heads the K9 unit.

Supe: “The threat comes with the job.”

LINK: SO WHEN YOU DIAL 10111, THESE MAY BE THE POLICE OFFICERS THAT WILL COME TO AID YOU.
SUBTITLE
Vilakazi: “Cuffs!”
Maharaj: “Open the Fucking door, how long does it take to open the bloody door!” (bleep)
Nike: “I was almost dead...it was hell.”

SHABEEN - 23:00 Univille, Lenasia South, Sunday
SHOW: Nike, Rabbit, Blue and Zulu This unit gave Carte Blanche exclusive behind-the-scenes access for a month to observe the officers in action.

UPSOUND: “Don’t move, don’t move.” We call them Nike, Rabbit, Blue and Zulu - hiding their identities to protect them in the line of duty.

Supe int: “I think the most important thing is gaining trust back from the public.”Historically, municipal police forces have had a bad reputation for corruption. The JMPD was created in 2001 to assist the National Police force in fighting crime in the city.

Drugs in guy’s mouth 21:00 Robertsham, Saturday UPSOUND: “He swallowed this stuff this S***t…” (bleep) I know this f***er, I know.”
18:00 Parade, Friday

Every shift starts with a briefing where Supe details the day’s planned operations. The unit has 6 rotating shifts that operate 24-hours a day, every day of the year. Supe is on near constant call.

Supe: “Some of my members say I never sleep, or that I sleep with the radio under my pillow. If they need me, I need to be there.”
Nike Each shift is run by a Sergeant, like Nike, who has spent his entire career in the K9 Unit.
– nike in vehicle -

SUBTITLE Nike: “This job is a calling. You must have a passion. Yes, sometimes our life is at risk. But it's part of our job.”
visuals of rico and sheeba Like most officers, Sergeant Nike relies heavily on his canine partner, a narcotics dog named Sheeba.
As does fellow officer Tyrone Moitze…

Tyrone Moitze:“He makes me smile everyday.”
Wolf His canine partner Wolf is trained to respond only to his call.

Tyrone Tyrone: “It’s like I was his mate. He’s my back up when I’m out there on the street.”
VIDEO OF SUPE AND SASHA Supe: “The animal or the dog is considered a police official. Anything that you do to the handler you do to the dog. You’ll be charged.”

15:00, Thursday Driving car.
Aside from planned operations, the unit is primed for incoming calls… They’re called to a chop shop and race to the scene.
Racing to a scene


Get out car at scene MAC: “THIS IS PROBABLY ONE OF THE MOST EXHILARATING THINGS IN MY ENTIRE LIFE. THIS IS WHAT IT FEELS LIKE TO BE IN A POLICE CAR WHEN THEY’RE EITHER APPREHENDING OR CHASING A CRIMINAL.”
On the scene SUBTITLE

15:20 Finetown, Thursday Supe: “Is it only the bakke?” Vehicles like this one are stolen for spare parts...

LINK MAC: “FOR ME THE MOST INCREDIBLE THING IS THAT WITHIN 15 MINUTES THIS IS WHAT THE CAR LOOKS LIKE, IT’S STRIPPED TOTALLY BARE AND NOTHING TO FIND, AND THIS IS IDEALLY WHAT HAPPENS TO YOUR CAR, WHEN IT GETS STOLEN.”
18:00 Soweto, Thursday While Jozi residents are having dinner... the unit gets a tip-off about stolen firearms.
on scene

SEE BAGS and recovered stuff 21:00 Snake Park, Soweto Thursday Mac: “ So Police have been able to find the suspect, he was in the house, and they also found jammers in and around the property…the weapons are not at this premises, so we have to go to another premises...
Mac: “Come in, come see here.” electronics It’s a massive haul of electronics scattered across every room - all stolen from cars.

Mac: “So fortunately this is one of the guns which was found, with the great work of the police further crimes can’t be committed with this stolen weapon.”

LINK 01:00 Soweto, Thursday THIS IS THE KIND OF ACTION NECESSARY TO PREVENT CRIME, BUT IT OFTEN LEADS TO THE POLICE THEMSELVES BECOMING TARGETS.

Zulu: “I was shot in the chest, the bullet went right through the bullet proof vest, in the chest.”

Zulu slomo intro Last year, Officer Zulu stared death in the face, when he responded to a call about a hijacked vehicle.

Zulu: “You can’t tell your wife or your kids that I’ll see you when I come back. You just say ‘goodbye,’ not knowing whether you’re going to come back or not.”

Supe: “My worst fear is responding to a scene where it’s one of your own that has been injured or murdered.”

JMPD officer death scene
23:00 Vlakfontein, Sunday And that fear came true when they attended this crime scene - a JMPD officer had been shot dead.
Supe Supe: “It’s actually difficult to accept, not that we don’t feel for any other scene that we go to, but JMPD is a close knit family.”
LINK


SUPE THE PHYSICAL DANGER IS NOT THE ONLY COST TO THIS JOB. MANY OF THESE OFFICERS TOLD US THE JOB TAKES A SEVERE EMOTIONAL TOLL. AND THIS IS THE THING THAT IS QUITE DIFFICULT FOR THEIR FAMILIES TO UNDERSTAND.

Supe: “A few years ago, we targeted a drug kingpin in the Hillbrow area, and there was threats at home, so the family had to go for two months into safekeeping.”
Nike
SUBTITLE

Nike: “If people who are not in the police environment, it's not easy for them to understand. It’s like people always think why are police officers shooting themselves. it’s the stress that we have to deal with and people don’t want to go for counseling, because it looks like, that you are weak, you cannot handle stress.”

SHOT OF SANDTON fade
00:02 Alexandra, Friday
But every shift is stressful. Supe stops the patrol vehicle to break up a fight in Alexandra. He’s rewarded with a brick hurled at his body.
Rabbit
SUBTITLE Rabbit: “One question we get asked when we stop a vehicle, is do I look like a criminal? And then I usually respond by asking them, can you please tell me, how does a criminal look?”
Rabbit driving Officer Rabbit* joined the unit at its inception. He still finds that many Joburg residents assume the JMPD only hands out traffic tickets.

Rabbit intv
SUBTITLE
Rabbit: “Most of the criminals we arrest are very well-dressed, you won’t say this is a criminal.”
Rabbit driving
Rabbit shields his family from the details of every shift’s risks. He attributes the unit’s safety record to their low profile.

Rabbit intv
SUBTITLE Rabbit: “With the unmarked vehicle and driving in civilian clothes, you can actually stand next to the suspect, and we sit there and we wait, and before they strike, we usually try and prevent it from happening.”

show her with her dog

18:00 Zakariya Park, Friday

SUBTITLE But crime cannot always be prevented. Officer Blue - one of a handful of women in the unit - responds to a scene where two women have been killed during a house robbery.
Blue walks in and see body’s.
Blue: “Oh F**k.” (Bleep)

SUBTITLE
Pappas: “The husband came from work and he found his wife murdered with their helper. That’s when he noticed that the car is gone, so then he phoned his tracking company, the tracking company alerted the police.”

At the scene

19:00 Braamfontein, Friday


20:00 M1 highway joburg city, Friday

Nats sound...
The unit tracks down the victims’ stolen car. They arrest the driver, who divulges that his partner who committed the murders is headed to Limpopo. The JMPD’s swift action leads them to a taxi on the highway where he’s arrested.

Officer: “Handcuffs.”
Blue: “He’s confessing, saying that he’s the one who strangled both of them with electrical chords.”
As a wife and mother, Officer Blue says she struggles to balance job and family commitments.
Blue subtitle Blue: “The husband is always complaining You never have time to be at home. I don't have time to be a mother, because I'm an officer. This is a calling, you know. It’s something you love.”

LINK MAC: THIS JOB IS NOT EASY, ESPECIALLY WHEN YOU HAVE TO ENFORCE THE LAW. IT CAN GET ROUGH, BUT THIS JOB NEEDS TO BE DONE...
LIST STARTS In our month on the beat, we observe the K9 unit tracking and recovering stolen vehicles.

20:00 Orange Farm, Thursday
SUBTITLE

Linx: “The vehicle was hijacked in Vanderbijlpark, we managed to apprehend one, the other one jumped over the walls.”

Vilakazi: “You see? They m****d (BLEEP) it with a brick.”
LIST The unit makes arrests virtually every day.

fade
21:00 Soweto Hostels, Sunday


SUBTITLE
Fade Vilakazi: “Cuffs!”
The team caughts these alleged car thieves red-handed...

NATS sound
Sasha: “This is the key?”

Sitzwe: “Yes, It was from this guy.”
While leaving, a shot from an unknown location rings out.

Gun shot
22:00 Pimville, soweto , Sunday An hour later, the team arrests 3 more hijacking suspects…
Last month’s statistics from the unit speak for themselves...
Supe intv Supe: “We have had 15 firearms taken off the street with uh 52 recovered hijacked and stolen vehicles.”
LIST And these successes keep them going...as they battle to confiscate drugs and pursues the dealers.

15:00 Jeppe, Saturday
SUBTITLE

fade Nike: What are you selling? Take it out,

Natta: Sergeant, let him just take it out,

Nike: Nyaope?

Suspect: Yes.

23:00 Hillbrow, Friday To prevent crime from festering unchecked, the unit raids ownerless, hijacked buildings.
19:00 Braamfontein, Friday

Show him taking it out jacket

Drugs are often well hidden... but the canine partners are trained for these moments.
(Good boy!)
police kicking in door…
SUBTITLE Kick down door
Officer: “Where’s your passports?”

JMPD spokesperson wayne minnaar Wayne: “Tonight we arrested 27 persons who are undocumented and are being kept at hillbrow station, and found 108 satchels of dagga was also discovered.”

LIST Recovering stolen or illegal firearms is a priority so they can’t be used in other crimes.
22:00 Klipspruit, Sunday

The team pulls over a wanted suspect...
Guys: “Got it Poes!!! (bleep)”

It’s a win! They find his stolen weapon.
LIST But their main mandate is to prevent or respond to violent crime.
Supe getting ready
(add in sound) gun clicking….


CCTV

SUBTITLE
Chase and recover vehicle This CCTV footage shows a robbery in progress. K9 is sent to pursue - it’s a gang of 15 suspects that flee on foot and start shooting at Rabbit and Nike. Hearing the shots, Supe gives chase.

SOUNDUP: Supe: “ Shots fired.”
Officers recover a vehicle with remnants of the stolen liquor in the boot. Nike has barely escaped the shoot-out with his life.

Nike
SUBTITLE Nike: “This is the one who was shooting us, shooting at me. I was almost dead, as I down, he started shooting. It was hell…”
pictures

One suspect dies on the scene. A few weeks later, the team apprehends the rest of the group.
Rabbit PAUSE/music/visual segue

Rabbit: “In a gunfight. If you walk away and you survived, it's a win for us.”

Nike
SUBTITLE PAUSE/music/visual segue
Nike: “ What can we do, you can only say thank-you for the Lord, that He has saved you, I don’t know for how long, but we never know, I'm here for a reason, to protect and serve people. ”

High speed chase - montage of action... SUBTITLE: Johannesburg is a bustling city open for business, but that attracts criminals who target its residents... While most sleep, members of the JMPD’s crack K9 unit leave their homes and families to patrol the city’s streets to prevent these criminals from taking over. Sikalala: Don’t ask me questions! F**k (bleep) you! With a long waiting list of officers who want to join their ranks, the K9 unit of Johannesburg’s Metro Police Department specializes in crime prevention. Supe: “We are quite close to our target.”show bedroom visuals here THEN LEAD INTO THE HERO VISUALS Super-in-tendent Mahomed Hoosen - called Supe - joined the police in his twenties. A father of two, he wanted to make the city safe for his family. He now heads the K9 unit. Supe: “The threat comes with the job.” LINK: SO WHEN YOU DIAL 10111, THESE MAY BE THE POLICE OFFICERS THAT WILL COME TO AID YOU. SUBTITLE Vilakazi: “Cuffs!” Maharaj: “Open the Fucking door, how long does it take to open the bloody door!” (bleep) Nike: “I was almost dead...it was hell.” SHABEEN - 23:00 Univille, Lenasia South, Sunday SHOW: Nike, Rabbit, Blue and Zulu This unit gave Carte Blanche exclusive behind-the-scenes access for a month to observe the officers in action. UPSOUND: “Don’t move, don’t move.” We call them Nike, Rabbit, Blue and Zulu - hiding their identities to protect them in the line of duty. Supe int: “I think the most important thing is gaining trust back from the public.”Historically, municipal police forces have had a bad reputation for corruption. The JMPD was created in 2001 to assist the National Police force in fighting crime in the city. Drugs in guy’s mouth 21:00 Robertsham, Saturday UPSOUND: “He swallowed this stuff this S***t…” (bleep) I know this f***er, I know.” 18:00 Parade, Friday Every shift starts with a briefing where Supe details the day’s planned operations. The unit has 6 rotating shifts that operate 24-hours a day, every day of the year. Supe is on near constant call. Supe: “Some of my members say I never sleep, or that I sleep with the radio under my pillow. If they need me, I need to be there.” Nike Each shift is run by a Sergeant, like Nike, who has spent his entire career in the K9 Unit. – nike in vehicle - SUBTITLE Nike: “This job is a calling. You must have a passion. Yes, sometimes our life is at risk. But it's part of our job.” visuals of rico and sheeba Like most officers, Sergeant Nike relies heavily on his canine partner, a narcotics dog named Sheeba. As does fellow officer Tyrone Moitze… Tyrone Moitze:“He makes me smile everyday.” Wolf His canine partner Wolf is trained to respond only to his call. Tyrone Tyrone: “It’s like I was his mate. He’s my back up when I’m out there on the street.” VIDEO OF SUPE AND SASHA Supe: “The animal or the dog is considered a police official. Anything that you do to the handler you do to the dog. You’ll be charged.” 15:00, Thursday Driving car. Aside from planned operations, the unit is primed for incoming calls… They’re called to a chop shop and race to the scene. Racing to a scene Get out car at scene MAC: “THIS IS PROBABLY ONE OF THE MOST EXHILARATING THINGS IN MY ENTIRE LIFE. THIS IS WHAT IT FEELS LIKE TO BE IN A POLICE CAR WHEN THEY’RE EITHER APPREHENDING OR CHASING A CRIMINAL.” On the scene SUBTITLE 15:20 Finetown, Thursday Supe: “Is it only the bakke?” Vehicles like this one are stolen for spare parts... LINK MAC: “FOR ME THE MOST INCREDIBLE THING IS THAT WITHIN 15 MINUTES THIS IS WHAT THE CAR LOOKS LIKE, IT’S STRIPPED TOTALLY BARE AND NOTHING TO FIND, AND THIS IS IDEALLY WHAT HAPPENS TO YOUR CAR, WHEN IT GETS STOLEN.” 18:00 Soweto, Thursday While Jozi residents are having dinner... the unit gets a tip-off about stolen firearms. on scene SEE BAGS and recovered stuff 21:00 Snake Park, Soweto Thursday Mac: “ So Police have been able to find the suspect, he was in the house, and they also found jammers in and around the property…the weapons are not at this premises, so we have to go to another premises... Mac: “Come in, come see here.” electronics It’s a massive haul of electronics scattered across every room - all stolen from cars. Mac: “So fortunately this is one of the guns which was found, with the great work of the police further crimes can’t be committed with this stolen weapon.” LINK 01:00 Soweto, Thursday THIS IS THE KIND OF ACTION NECESSARY TO PREVENT CRIME, BUT IT OFTEN LEADS TO THE POLICE THEMSELVES BECOMING TARGETS. Zulu: “I was shot in the chest, the bullet went right through the bullet proof vest, in the chest.” Zulu slomo intro Last year, Officer Zulu stared death in the face, when he responded to a call about a hijacked vehicle. Zulu: “You can’t tell your wife or your kids that I’ll see you when I come back. You just say ‘goodbye,’ not knowing whether you’re going to come back or not.” Supe: “My worst fear is responding to a scene where it’s one of your own that has been injured or murdered.” JMPD officer death scene 23:00 Vlakfontein, Sunday And that fear came true when they attended this crime scene - a JMPD officer had been shot dead. Supe Supe: “It’s actually difficult to accept, not that we don’t feel for any other scene that we go to, but JMPD is a close knit family.” LINK SUPE THE PHYSICAL DANGER IS NOT THE ONLY COST TO THIS JOB. MANY OF THESE OFFICERS TOLD US THE JOB TAKES A SEVERE EMOTIONAL TOLL. AND THIS IS THE THING THAT IS QUITE DIFFICULT FOR THEIR FAMILIES TO UNDERSTAND. Supe: “A few years ago, we targeted a drug kingpin in the Hillbrow area, and there was threats at home, so the family had to go for two months into safekeeping.” Nike SUBTITLE Nike: “If people who are not in the police environment, it's not easy for them to understand. Supe stops the patrol vehicle to break up a fight in Alexandra. He’s rewarded with a brick hurled at his body. Rabbit SUBTITLE Rabbit: “One question we get asked when we stop a vehicle, is do I look like a criminal? And then I usually respond by asking them, can you please tell me, how does a criminal look?” Rabbit driving Officer Rabbit* joined the unit at its inception. He still finds that many Joburg residents assume the JMPD only hands out traffic tickets. Rabbit intv SUBTITLE Rabbit: “Most of the criminals we arrest are very well-dressed, you won’t say this is a criminal.” Rabbit driving Rabbit shields his family from the details of every shift’s risks. He attributes the unit’s safety record to their low profile. Rabbit intv SUBTITLE Rabbit: “With the unmarked vehicle and driving in civilian clothes, you can actually stand next to the suspect, and we sit there and we wait, and before they strike, we usually try and prevent it from happening.” show her with her dog 18:00 Zakariya Park, Friday SUBTITLE But crime cannot always be prevented. Blue: “Oh F**k.” (Bleep) SUBTITLE Pappas: “The husband came from work and he found his wife murdered with their helper. The JMPD’s swift action leads them to a taxi on the highway where he’s arrested. Officer: “Handcuffs.” Blue: “He’s confessing, saying that he’s the one who strangled both of them with electrical chords.” As a wife and mother, Officer Blue says she struggles to balance job and family commitments. metadata.Unique Selling Point: STORY OUTLINE and TREATMENT So we all think the JMPD are corrupt traffic cops who wreck their cars. But here’s where you’re wrong - the metro cops actually have several tactical reaction and crime prevention units - one of them is the K9 unit - the one with the longest wait list and where all the tops cops are. We embedded with this unit for a month to see how they are protecting us. Their offices are hidden in nearby their headquarters in joburg city, there are roughly 6 teams (Alpha, bravo, charlie, delta, echo 1 and echo 2.) - lead by SuperIntendent Mahomed Hussein - he will be our main character. With more than 20 years in the force, he commands the respect of his peers as well as Chief Khanyile. His family have had to go into hiding, he’s been shot at, attacked and combatted nearly every crime joburg has to offer. Because of the nature of their work some of the officers from the Echo Units will need to be hidden, but they have consented to us filming their lower jaws to see them speaking, and with all the action I don’t think it’s something that detracts from the story. The echo units are the top cops - they are plain clothed officers who also move in unmarked vehicles which allows them to move in on the criminals easier than the other 4 units who are uniformed.
metadata.Summary: We will have a link with Macfarlane where we say that we are being responsible and want to protect these officers as some of them like another one of our main characters “Rabbit” are being targeted by criminals they have been brought to book. Rabbit’s nephew was murdered because of him arresting some criminals, and they have planned two hits on him since. He has a wicked sense of humour, but is often in all the action - with 15 years experience - he is one of the best in echo 1. Then there is Links - Lincoln Moloi - from echo 2, he is a spokesperson at every scene and always comes prepared. He often works double shifts and is one of the most dedicated officers - a little shy, but trusted by the community - he is known for always having information from informers and being first on the scene. “Nike” - he is the sergeant of echo 2 - 15 years experience, he has been with the unit since its inception and leads the pack from the front. He is known as the top dog, he always travels with Sheeba his border collie who he calls a police officer. He can be emotional, but is a protector - who has 4 daughters and bears the responsibility of doing all the paperwork, as well as being front and centre on most scenes. Besides these 3 of echo 1 and 2 - there are others who appear in the story - Younos and Papas - known as the terrible twins or bac-and-teria. Magubane and Sitzwe - another unbreakable partnership. Vilakazi, Vence, Zwane and Natta (a female indian officer who roles with the boys).
metadata.Further information: Then the officers who are uniformed - “Cherry Pie” - who is a tough female officer who takes no nonsense and decided to leave the echo units to become a uniformed officer because it requires a 24.7 approach. She has been with the unit roughly 14 years and her Golden Retriever Fire is a stud when it comes to competing, as well as sniffing out narcotics. Then there is Tyrone Moitze - a 6.8 towering giant. He and his german shepherd wolf are one of my main characters, he speaks to camera without hidden identity and is loveable and hard working. Wolf sniffs out the guns and explosives at most scenes. We see his dog working, as well as competing. They really are a lovable pair. Then there is the Seppi - Saregent September who heads all the training of the dogs. His office is adorned with every award a dog trainer could ever behold and is fierce when it comes to whats best for his working animals. Theme: broken window approach: We meet them at the mayors office - the members are briefed by super intendent mahomed hussein, and his sergeant - Nike. They are told that we are conducting a raid on an inner city hijacked building where the nearby business owners have complained about drug dealers illegally occupying and living in the building. We go in kicking in doors, searching suspects with the dogs. We recover several drugs with cooper a narcotics dog. We have great footage of searching the suspects etc. This is one of several operations in which the JMPD lead there members into treacherous and unknown circumstances. This is all part of the city’s call to clean up it’s streets - something that is hard to do because of a lack of resources like vehicles, red tape surrounding the laws allowing officers to protect themselves and of course the fact that Joburg is overrun with gangs who hijack vehicles, plague houses by robbing them and now a new crime - kidnapping. On another night, we raid several johannesburg buildings - find drugs, and over 50 illegals are sent to lindela. We have footage of the illegals being put into vans - its very sad - then we show their living conditions - which are horrendous. We then break down the door of the one room, and a guy jumps out the window. He’s the one on the news that died. Theme: Often police are targeted: like when a member house was targeted and his firearm was stolen (CCTV footage), we got information about the cars locations through informers, so we watched the car for two nights - and then we caught them with the gun - nice footage of arrests. They track cell phones - and we recovered a police cellphone that was stolen in KZN in soweto - we then searched the suspects house for the gun. We used Moitze and Wolf who sniffs throughout the house looking for the weapon. A police officer was attacked in joburg for his firearm, three days later after observation we manage to catch the criminals with the firearm after a chase. Very exciting footage. Then one night we get the call that a fellow JMPD officer has been targeted and shot dead. Supe gives a very emotional speech about this, and we will hear from Rabbit about how he has these hits out for him. Theme: Crime Prevention: What most people don’t know is that Echo 1 and 2 are crime prevention experts - riding around every day and night fighting crime before it happens - like in the case of the armed robbery we were all seemingly prepared to stop before we ran into it and there was a shoot out, in which rabbit and nike emptied their clips within minutes. Nike gave chase on foot, while Rabbit tried to catch one of the gettaway vehicles. By the end of the explosive fight, two suspects died from bullet wounds and the boys survived - just barely to catch the cars and recover the alcohol. Rabbit and Nike were very emotional afterwards having just had a gun fight with roughly 15 armed suspects - they will talk us through what happened, and we also have the CCTV footage and chase following the shootout. I mean seriously!
